:::{#def-prediction-bias}
#### Bias of a prediction

Let $\fitproc$ be a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure),
and let $\trainset$ be a random [training set](#def-training-set).
At a covariate value $\predvar$,
the prediction $\predvalf{\predvar}$ is a random variable,
because it depends on the random training data.
Let $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$ be a [new observation](#def-new-observation) with $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
The **bias** of the prediction
is the expected [prediction error](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error)
of the prediction $\predvalf{\predvar}$ of the new outcome $\newoutvar$.
The expectation averages over [training sets](#def-training-set) and over the new outcome:

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \E{\prederr_{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias}

The new observation is independent of the training set.
So by the [law of iterated expectations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-lie),
the expectation can be taken in two steps:
first over the new outcome with the training set fixed,
then over the training sets.

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \Expfc{\trainset}{\Expfc{\newoutvar}{\prederr_{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \trainset, \newpredvar = \predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias-iterated}

The [training set](#def-training-set) consists of $\nobs$ [independent and identically distributed](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-iid) pairs $\paren{\Predvar_\iobs, \Outvar_\iobs}$,
so its density is the product of the densities of its pairs.
When the variables are continuous, the two steps are integrals.
The inner integral runs over the new outcome $\outvar$,
and the outer integral runs over the values $\paren{\predvar_\iobs, \outvar_\iobs}$ of the training pairs,
which determine the prediction $\predvalf{\predvar}$:

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \int \cdots \int
\paren{\int \paren{\predvalf{\predvar} - \outvar} \p(\newoutvar = \outvar \mid \newpredvar = \predvar) \, d\outvar}
\prod_{\iobs = 1}^{\nobs} \p(\Predvar_\iobs = \predvar_\iobs,\, \Outvar_\iobs = \outvar_\iobs)
\, d\predvar_1 \, d\outvar_1 \cdots d\predvar_\nobs \, d\outvar_\nobs.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias-integral}

For discrete variables, the integrals are sums.

This expected error is signed, not squared.
It is not the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-prediction-bias-average-fit}
#### The bias as the expected prediction minus the mean function

The [bias](#def-prediction-bias) of the [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) at $\predvar$
is the [expected prediction](#def-average-fit) minus the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value:

$$
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \Epredval - \truemeanf{\predvar}.
$$ {#eq-prediction-bias-average-fit}

:::

::: proof

The new outcome is [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of the [training set](#def-training-set),
and its mean is $\truemeanf{\predvar}$ because the [noise has mean zero](#thm-noise-mean-zero).

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}
&= \E{\prederr_{*}\paren{\fitmodf{\trainset}} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar} && \text{(definition of bias)} \\
&= \E{\devof{\predvalf{\predvar}}{\newoutvar}} && \text{(definition of prediction error)} \\
&= \Epredval - \E{\newoutvar} && \text{(linearity of expectation)} \\
&= \Epredval - \truemeanf{\predvar} && \text{(the noise has mean zero)} .
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

In expected prediction error decompositions [@james2021islr2e, Section 2.2.2],
the bias reflects the approximation error that comes from approximating a real-world relationship by a model.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-prediction-bias}
#### Computing the bias of a prediction

Suppose $\truemeanf{\predvar} = 10$,
and the predictions $\predvalf{\predvar}$,
over repeated training sets,
average $11$.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\predval}
&= \Epredval - \truemeanf{\predvar} && \text{(@thm-prediction-bias-average-fit)} \\
&= 11 - 10 \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The squared bias is $1^2 = 1$,
the value in @exr-epe-three-sources.

:::
